text:
At five in the evening


I had already spent eight days with my boots split

because of the pebbles; and I arrived at Charleroi.

At the Green Cabaret I ordered slices of toast

with butter and juicy, warming ham.


I stretched both legs out, happy, under the green

table, while I looked at the naive drawings

of the wallpaper. What joy when the little maid,

the one with big breasts and eyes like embers


—she, yes, is not frightened by a simple kiss—,

laughing, offered me toast with butter

and warm ham, on a many-colored plate!


White and pink ham perfuming a clove

of garlic; and she filled my enormous mug: foam

that gilded the glow of an almost sleeping sun.

translation.title: At the Green Cabaret
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the hungry traveler's tavern relief, earthy sensuality, and late-afternoon glow.
